chapter: Chicago pianists and New Orleans bands
title: Tony Jackson, Pretty Baby, and Chicago pianists and the Pekin Theater
summary: Jackson wrote Pretty Baby in Chicago around 1911-12; Compton names other pianists and the Pekin Theater where his wife starred.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: In 1904. In 1904. I met Tony. Was he writing pieces himself? Did he have his own pieces those days?

No, he didn't have them in those days. He didn't start them until later on in Chicago, around 11, 1911 and 12. He was playing at the Elite number two because I was playing at the Elite number one. And Tony wrote Pretty Baby. Nothing like you ever heard it though.
Different words. You sang some of those words one time. Yes.

There's a certain girl in my neighborhood that I certainly am crazy about. In a certain way she stole my heart one day. And it's hers without a doubt. Now the other day while on my way just for a quiet stroll, I met this girl with brain of oil. Speaking of her jelly roll. She looked at me inside and then she gently replied. I gently replied. You may talk about your jelly rolls but none of them compare with my baby. My pretty baby. She's a tall doggy. I would be brown eyes and curly hair. I call her baby. My pretty baby. Maybe not today but there'll come a time when you hear those church bells chime. Kings and queens may reign supreme but none of them outshine this pretty baby of mine. That was his first lyrics. And actually when he sold it, he got some professional lyric writers to write some real lyrics for him.
It's ordinary. What was Tony like when you first met him? Was he a good pianist or did he sing most of the time?

He was a very good pianist, yeah. He always was good. We had some good ones here then. Oscar Holden, Tony Jackson, Clarence Jones, Ed Harden. Ed played at the Peekin Theater, 2700 State. That's where my wife and Lottie Grady was starred. Nettie Lewis and Lottie Grady. Your wife's name was Lewis? Nettie Lewis then. She wasn't my wife then. No. No. And Lottie Grady now she's got a tavern in Idlewild, Michigan.
Was the Peekin Theater then? Yes. Did they have the theater?
Was there a nightclub there too at that time?
No. Just the theater. Just the theater. Lightclub opened later.
